title: When there's no water
hookLine: a clean earth or dust wipe of face and hands replaces washing (5:6)

lines: A NECKLACE LOST IN THE DESERT.
NO WATER, AND THE PRAYER TIME COMES.
A VERSE, AND THE NECKLACE UNDER THE CAMEL.
cards: A necklace goes missing in the desert. Aishah has lost it on a journey, and the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, stops the caravan to look for it. But the place they've stopped has no water, and they're carrying none.
The prayer time comes. People go to Aishah's father, Abu Bakr, and complain: look what she's done. Abu Bakr comes and scolds her, while the Prophet ﷺ sleeps with his head on her lap.
Then a verse comes down. And when they finally move her camel, there's the necklace, lying underneath it. Sahih al-Bukhari tells it, at number 334.

teach.h: NO WATER: GO TO CLEAN EARTH.
teach.b: Year one met the word tayammum; today, its story and its steps. The verse is the end of 5:6, the same verse that gave wudu and ghusl.
It says that if you are sick, or on a journey, or have come from relieving yourself or been intimate, and you find no water, then go to clean earth and wipe your faces and your hands with it.

teach.h: NOT A BURDEN, BUT A PURIFYING.
teach.b: Then, in Pickthall's translation: "Allah would not place a burden on you, but He would purify you." That's the spirit of the ruling. The water ran out, and the prayer didn't.
In the story, a companion named Usayd ibn Hudayr said this wasn't the first blessing to come through Abu Bakr's family: a lost necklace became an easing for everyone after. How is it done?
In Sahih al-Bukhari, number 338, a companion, Ammar ibn Yasir, needed a full bath on a journey with no water.
He didn't know about tayammum yet, so he rolled in the dust like an animal, and prayed.

teach.h: STRIKE, BLOW, WIPE FACE AND HANDS.
teach.b: When he told the Prophet ﷺ, he was shown something much simpler: strike the earth with your hands, blow on them, wipe your face and your hands.
The schools differ on details, one strike or two, the hands to the wrist or further, but the shape is the same, and it stands in for wudu and ghusl alike.

teach.h: ALLAH WOULD NOT PLACE A BURDEN ON YOU.
teach.b: In Bukhari 335, the Prophet ﷺ says the earth has been made for him a place of prayer and a means of purification. Water, when there is water. Clean earth, when there isn't.

how: When Muslims have no water, or water would harm them through illness, they make tayammum: they strike clean earth or dust with their hands and wipe the face and hands, then pray; it stands in for both wudu and ghusl until water is available.

o: washing with sand instead of soap before every meal
washing with milk or juice when the water runs out
wiping face and hands with clean earth when there's no water

games.q: when there's no water — tap the pairs.
p: strike, blow, wipe face and hands
the earth, a means of purification

s: tayammum means wiping the whole body with dust
Ammar tried that. he was shown: strike the earth, blow, wipe the face and hands.
tayammum can stand in for ghusl as well as wudu
Ammar needed a full bath, and tayammum was what he was shown.
the verse of tayammum came after a lost necklace
Bukhari 334: the caravan stopped to search, with no water, and the verse came.

games.q: Ammar ibn Yasir is on a journey, needing a full bath, and there's no water anywhere. he's never heard of tayammum. what did he do?
o: skip the prayer until you find water.
roll in the dust from head to foot, then pray.
games.why: he rolled in the dust like an animal. the Prophet showed him something far simpler: strike the earth, blow, wipe face and hands.

practice: Rest your palms flat on whatever is beneath you and feel how ordinary that surface is.
Slowly lift your hands and, in your mind, wipe your face with them once, then wipe the back of one hand with the other, and switch: that's the shape of tayammum.
If you don't pray, sit with the idea in it: when the usual way is closed, there's still a way.

wordCard.voice: Tayammum. The dry purification: clean earth, the face and the hands, in place of water when there's none or it would harm you. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the dry purification with clean earth.

carryVoice: Your line: the earth is clean. Even dust can be a way in. See you tomorrow, at the call.
